Commentary.Commentary: We are back for South Africa's reply. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Ryan Rickelton and Aiden Markram to open for the visitors. The Eagle, Shaheen Afridi, to bowl first. Lets go...
...SECOND INNINGS...

Salman Agha was stranded at the other end, watching it fall apart, but he too lost his patience as he departed 7 short of his century. Pakistan had a real chance of scoring around 450 but a small collapse, which happened twice in the innings, didn't help their cause. Apart from that, the hosts batted really well with the stand between Imam-ul-Haq and Shan Masood early on, and later, the partnership between Mohammad Rizwan and Salman Agha was the highlight of the innings. Now, South Africa have momentum on their side but they have to be cautious with how the pitch is behaving. It won't be easy for them as well. Can the Proteas handle the Asian conditions? Let's find out.

Senuran Muthusamy takes the catch and keeps it with himself. He will cherish it forever. A maiden sixth-wicket haul for the spinner and he has single-handedly dismantled the Pakistani side. From 313/5, Pakistan are bowled out for 378. The home team started the day well with Mohammad Rizwan and Salman Agha picking up right from where they left off on Day 1. The duo batted well before Mohammad Rizwan nicked one behind the stumps to Senuran Muthusamy. That wicket brought two more prized wickets as Noman Ali and Sajid Khan followed him in the same over to create havoc in the middle.

OUT! GONE! Salman Agha loses patience as he falls on 93. Tossed up no middle, Salman Agha dances down the track to heave across the line, hits it to deep mid-wicket where Senuran Muthusamy takes it. Pakistan are all out for 378.

For South Africa, the task is clear. Break this partnership swiftly. Their spin unit, which accounted for four of the five wickets to fall, will once again be key on this pitch. An early breakthrough is essential to expose the tail and restrict Pakistan’s score. Will Pakistan pile on the runs, or can the Proteas orchestrate another dramatic collapse? We shall find out...

The final session belonged entirely to the unflappable Mohammad Rizwan and Agha Salman. Their unbeaten 114-run partnership took Pakistan to stumps with the twin half-centuries, turning a potential disaster into a position of strength. Both men will be eyeing centuries this morning, looking to bat deep and push the total past the 450-run mark to set a truly challenging total.

The story of Day 1 was one of resilience and partnership. After a disastrous start saw the early loss of Abdullah Shafique, it was the superb 161-run stand between Shan Masood and a determined Imam-ul-Haq that stabilized the innings. However, a middle-order wobble saw Pakistan lose four quick wickets for just 36 runs, with the Proteas’ spin trio, led by Senuran Muthusamy, making a decisive fightback to leave the hosts reeling at 199/5.

Welcome back for Day 2 of what has been a thrilling Test match so far! After a captivating opening day that saw momentum swing wildly, we are set for another day of high-stakes cricket as Pakistan resumes its first innings from a commanding position of 313/5.

Earlier, Pakistan chose to bat first and lost Abdullah Shafique in the very first over but Shan Masood and Imam-ul-Haq turned things around with a wonderful partnership. South Africa relied mostly on their spinners to find breakthroughs and did well to keep a stem on the runflow. However, the way things went, it was the hosts who ended on a high note. What's in there for Day 2? Well, Pakistan are in firm control and will look to control the proceedings. The first thing South Africa will do is look for the breakthrough. Join us back at 5 am GMT for all the action of Day 2. Do join us earlier for the build up. Till then, cheers!

The spinners got a lot of turn and South Africa showcased good consistency to scalp some wickets.

A good closure to the game by the home team, and they'll be happy with how the final session has panned out. After the dramatic second session, where Pakistan lost three wickets, they needed a good, confident end to the day, and Mohammad Rizwan and Salman Agha supported the cause. However, South Africa stuck with spin as the game progressed, they unearthed a lot of turn off the surface, troubling the hosts a little. Masood and Imam-ul-Haq negotiated the spinners well until the former was trapped LBW. Babar Azam survived a scare as well, out caught behind but the decision was overturned through a review. But things got chaotic as Pakistan lost back-to-back wickets in the final over of the session. South Africa have the momentum as they go into the break. They'll look for more wickets as the spinners are settling in well. The game has come alive now. Stay tuned for the final session.

... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

There's loads to look forward to in the post-Lunch session. The batters will be aiming to pile on more runs and create a gap between them and the Proteas, with the pitch's tricky tendencies on their mind, while the bowlers will be desperate to grab wickets in a bunch and make up for the lacklustre session they've had. Plenty at stake. We'll be back at 7:42 am GMT.

The South African bowling has been pretty good. They're hitting decent lengths but they've been guilty of straying with the line occasionally, and that's exactly where they've leaked loads of runs in the first session. Kagiso Rabada grabbed the lone wicket in the very first over and they've been struggling to contain runs ever since. It's a track that's going to help the spinners, but even they need to hit the right areas. A few deliveries have landed nicely for the spinners but they've lacked consistency and that's where Pakistan have capitalised.

Despite the South African bowlers pitching in good areas, both Shan Masood and Imam-ul-Haq have done a fantastic job keeping the scoreboard moving by taking quick singles and displaying brilliant running between the wickets so far. The pair have respected the good deliveries but made sure no loose ones went unpunished. Boundaries have flowed easily for these two, and that's had a huge impact on Pakistan's standings right now.

After winning the toss and opting to bat first, Pakistan hadn't gotten off to the best start as Abdullah Shafique departed in the very first over itself. But the Pakistan captain, Shan Masood, walked in and made his intentions clear by smashing boundaries and not letting the bowler dictate terms. Imam-ul-Haq looked solid too, staying unbeaten on 59.

They're looking strong heading into the lunch break.

PITCH REPORT - Ramiz Raja and Bazid Khan are pitchside and Ramiz reckons that Pakistan won the toss and opted to bat first on a surface that looked abrasive. Bazid Khan also thinks that the pitch was still very dry, with cracks appearing on it right from the first morning itself, creating a situation where spinners could be effective. He further pointed out that in the landing area, there was a patch of grass compared to the rest of the pitch, which appeared brown. Both acknowledged that as the match progresses, the spinners will be expected to come into play even more. They emphasised the importance of establishing a solid first innings total as it would become tough to bat as the game went on.

Aiden Markram, the South Africa captain, expressed that he isn't nervous; instead, he sees it as an opportunity for his team to demonstrate their strength. Acknowledging the absence of Temba Bavuma and Keshav Maharaj from a leadership standpoint, Markram emphasised that they are keen to put up a stellar performance. Having put in rigorous training and focused on adapting to the conditions, he underscored that it ultimately boils down to having self-belief and trusting one's abilities.

Shan Masood, the Pakistan captain, mentioned that they will bat first. Highlighting their bowling strengths, he noted they have two spinners who can bowl exceptionally well, and alongside that, if the pitch offers cracks or conditions for reverse swing, they want to be well-equipped in the pace department too. Reckons that it is a massive opportunity for them to gauge themselves against the World Test Champions and display their skills against top-notch opposition.

Pakistan, on the other hand, will be led by Shan Masood with a strategy focused on a spin-heavy bowling attack – suiting their home conditions where turn is expected to play a big part. They’ve named five frontline spinners – Nauman Ali, Sajid Khan, Asif Afridi, Abrar Ahmed, and another, showcasing their intent to exploit the turning tracks. The hosts also have three uncapped players in their squad – Asif Afridi, Faisal Akram, and Rohail Nazir – with Afridi’s selection drawing attention due to his age of 38, making for a potential late debut. Shaheen Shah Afridi returns to the squad after a long absence, and Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan make their comeback after a two-month break.
